fixes.explanation: Mark 4:36 says the disciples took Jesus with them "…since He was already in the boat." So nobody had to fetch Him. They dismissed the crowd, and Jesus was already aboard. The boat was ready with Him in it.
No dock in this passage, friend. Mark 4:36 says they took Jesus with them "…since He was already in the boat." The text puts Him aboard already. Nobody had to meet Him anywhere.

Wading out sounds like a dramatic entrance, but that's not what happens. Mark 4:36 says they took Jesus with them "…since He was already in the boat." He was already aboard when they took Him along. No wading needed.

It's actually true. Mark 4:36 says, "And there were other boats with Him." The disciples weren't the only boat out on that water. The text doesn't say who, if anyone, was aboard those other boats, so I'll leave that one alone.
Mark 4:37 says the waves were breaking over the boat, "…so that it was being swamped." That's more water coming in than the boat can handle. I bet anybody on board wished they were somewhere calmer.

An anchor is for holding a boat in place, and that's not the word here. Mark 4:37 says the waves were breaking over it, "…so that it was being swamped." Swamped means filling with water. I think an anchor would have been the least of their worries.

Mark 4:39 says, "And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm." That came after He commanded, "Silence!" and "Be still!" No leftover wind is mentioned. A violent windstorm turned into perfectly calm.

The text doesn't describe a slow fade. Mark 4:39 says Jesus commanded the wind and sea, "And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm." There's no mention of it lasting through the night. It went from violent to perfectly calm after He spoke.

Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Do you still have no faith?" That's His second question, right after "Why are you so afraid?" Two questions, back to back. I think it's a question worth sitting with, friend.
Wisdom is a good thing, but it's not the word here. Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Do you still have no faith?" He's asking about faith, not wisdom.

Mark 4:41 says, "Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?" They said it overwhelmed with fear. The sea was calm, and the fear was still there. The text doesn't answer the question right there, so I'll leave it hanging too.
